findings.highlight: the estimated profit for a concert has jumped to twice the usual amount
findings.evidenceJa: 来日公演の提示額がいきなり倍に跳ね上がる
findings.explanation: The amount being offered for a Japanese performance has doubled. The translation turns a concrete offer made to Youko's office into an internally estimated profit, changing both the payer/payee relation and the certainty of the money.
findings.japanese:
「おかげで来日公演の提示額が
いきなり倍に跳ね上がるし…
今日本に行かないテはないのよ」
findings.todokanai: "Thanks to that, the estimated profit for a concert has jumped to twice the usual amount… There's just no way we can miss out on going to Japan right now."

findings.highlight: If I start looking for another route now, I might be late
findings.evidenceJa: 今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな
findings.explanation: Setsuna is waiting for the connecting bus and still has a transfer ahead of her, so she may arrive later. She is not searching for an alternate route.
findings.japanese:
「そっか…こっちは今、連絡バス待ち。
今から乗り継ぎだから、わたしの方が遅くなるかな…」
findings.todokanai: "Is that so… I'm still waiting for my bus. If I start looking for another route now, I might be late…"

findings.highlight: It's snowing really hard here in Paris.
findings.evidenceJa: パリがもう凄い雪でさ、今日中に着かないかと思ったよ
findings.explanation: Haruki has reached the station at his destination and says the snow in Paris was so severe he feared he would not arrive that day. 'Here in Paris' leaves him in the wrong city during the phone call.
findings.japanese:
「パリがもう凄い雪でさ、
今日中に着かないかと思ったよ」
findings.todokanai: "It's snowing really hard here in Paris. I didn't think I'd make it by today."

findings.highlight: The detailed information will be sent to you
findings.evidenceJa: 詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってある
findings.explanation: The attachment has already been sent to Haruki's computer email address, and he is instructed to read it carefully. The translation makes the delivery future and replaces the instruction with a summary statement.
findings.japanese:
『詳細はＰＣのメアドに添付ファイルで送ってあるから、
そっちをしっかり見ておくように。
とりあえずこちらは概要だけ』
findings.todokanai: "The detailed information will be sent to you in an attached file via email. I just want to summarize the most important points."

findings.highlight: what interaction will take place
findings.evidenceJa: どんな接点があったとしても
findings.explanation: Haruki resolves that whatever connection may already exist between pianist Kazusa and Kaiousha's Kitahara Haruki must not matter professionally. The future wording erases the dangerous shared past he is trying to bracket.
findings.japanese:
ピアニスト冬馬かずさと、開桜社北原春希の間に
どんな接点があったとしても…
findings.todokanai: No matter what interaction will take place between the pianist Touma Kazusa and Kitahara Haruki of Kaiousha…

findings.highlight: play the piano with such emotion
findings.evidenceJa: あんな色ボケたピアノが弾ける
findings.explanation: Youko marvels that her ascetic daughter can play such a lovesick or erotically infatuated piano. Generic 'emotion' sanitizes the pointed contradiction between Kazusa's outward severity and the desire exposed in her playing.
findings.japanese:
「ほんと、我が娘ながらストイックなコ…
それでよくもまぁあんな色ボケたピアノが弾けるわね」
findings.todokanai: "Oh dear, my daughter is a stoic… I'm amazed you can play the piano with such emotion when this is what you're like."

findings.highlight: the back of her feet
findings.evidenceJa: 足の裏や指の間まで念入りにぬぐう
findings.explanation: Haruki carefully wipes the soles of Kazusa's feet and between her toes. 足の裏 is the sole, not the top or back of the foot.
findings.japanese:
傷の回りの汚れを落とし、
それから足の裏や指の間まで念入りにぬぐう。
findings.todokanai: After cleaning away the dirt around her wound, I wipe the back of her feet and between her toes.

findings.highlight: bruised and scratched at the same time
findings.evidenceJa: 擦り傷と打ち身としもやけを一気にこさえる
findings.explanation: Haruki lists three simultaneous injuries: an abrasion, a bruise, and chilblains. The translation omits the cold injury, even though the following extended treatment is specifically about restoring warmth and circulation.
findings.japanese:
「擦り傷と打ち身としもやけを一気にこさえるからだ。
ほら、足こっち向けて。
しみると思うけど我慢しろよ」
findings.todokanai: "Only because you got yourself bruised and scratched at the same time. Come on, hold your leg out. This might sting a bit, but try to bear it."

findings.highlight: Once Kazusa finally calms down, I grab her foot and clean the wounded area with cotton containing disinfectant.
findings.evidenceJa:
ふてくされたようにやっと黙ったかずさの足を取り、
脱脂綿に含めた消毒薬を、
かかとの傷口につける。
findings.explanation: Kazusa has begun sulking after the alcohol stings; 'she's calmed down' reverses the emotional coloring.
findings.japanese:
ふてくされたようにやっと黙ったかずさの足を取り、
脱脂綿に含めた消毒薬を、
かかとの傷口につける。
findings.todokanai: Once Kazusa finally calms down, I grab her foot and clean the wounded area with cotton containing disinfectant.

findings.highlight: The courage to finally face the lingering feeling from my past.
findings.evidenceJa:
過去からの因縁に連なる思い出の魔女に、
最後の戦いを挑む勇気を。
findings.explanation: The memory-witch bound to fate from the past becomes an abstract lingering feeling, dropping Haruki's fantasy-adventure metaphor.
findings.japanese:
過去からの因縁に連なる思い出の魔女に、
最後の戦いを挑む勇気を。
findings.todokanai: The courage to finally face the lingering feeling from my past.

findings.highlight: I'm sure it won't be what Kazusa wants to hear
findings.evidenceJa: 何を答えても、それは多分かずさの聞きたかったことであり
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that whatever of the two possible questions he answers, it probably is something Kazusa wanted to ask—and also something he did not want to discuss. The translation negates the first proposition and substitutes 'want to hear' for 'wanted to ask.'
findings.japanese:
けど、何を答えても、それは多分
かずさの聞きたかったことであり…
findings.todokanai: But no matter what I answer, I'm sure it won't be what Kazusa wants to hear…

findings.highlight: I'm sure that this "a lot" includes Kazusa herself
findings.evidenceJa: かずさ自身は登場していたんだろうか
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether Kazusa herself appeared in the 'various things' she imagined behind his delayed relationship with Setsuna. The English asserts certainty where the Japanese sustains his uncertainty about her self-awareness.
findings.japanese:
その時、かずさが思い浮かべた『色々』に、
かずさ自身は登場していたんだろうか。
findings.todokanai: I'm sure that this "a lot" includes Kazusa herself in Kazusa's mind.

findings.highlight: She's even forgiven all that you've… All that I've done…
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に、本当にいいコだもんな、雪菜
findings.explanation: Kazusa only says that Setsuna is a truly, truly good girl. The English adds a complete self-correcting confession about what Haruki and Kazusa did, making implicit guilt explicit dialogue.
findings.japanese: 「本当に、本当にいいコだもんな、雪菜」
findings.todokanai: "Setsuna is a really, really good girl, after all. She's even forgiven all that you've… All that I've done…"

findings.highlight: And she won't run away… like I did…
findings.evidenceJa: 可愛くて、優しくて、心が綺麗で、一途で…
findings.explanation: Kazusa praises Setsuna as cute, kind, pure-hearted, and devoted, then trails off. The translation writes a new explicit comparison to Kazusa running away, again converting subtext into authored confession.
findings.japanese:
「世界中探しても、あんな素敵な恋人はいないぞ。
可愛くて、優しくて、心が綺麗で、一途で…」
findings.todokanai: "You couldn't find a better lover than her if you searched the whole world. She's adorable, kind, pure-hearted, and devoted… And she won't run away… like I did…"

findings.highlight: a languid feeling of uncertainty
findings.evidenceJa: 気怠い無常感みたいなのがじわじわと全身を覆う
findings.explanation: 無常感 here is a languid sense of impermanence, futility, or transience as the meeting ends, not uncertainty about what will happen. The mistranslation weakens the scene's terminal emotional atmosphere.
findings.japanese:
ただ、さっきのかずさの態度と同じように、
気怠い無常感みたいなのがじわじわと全身を覆う。
findings.todokanai: Instead, just like in Kazusa's case a short while ago, a languid feeling of uncertainty slowly permeates my body.

findings.highlight: My uncertainty flies away in an instant
findings.evidenceJa: 無常感は一瞬で吹き飛び
findings.explanation: This explicitly recalls the preceding sense of impermanence, which vanishes when Haruki learns there will be a tomorrow. Repeating 'uncertainty' breaks that emotional callback.
findings.japanese:
無常感は一瞬で吹き飛び、
様々な思いが頭の中をかき回すように飛び交った。
findings.todokanai: My uncertainty flies away in an instant, and various thoughts float around in my head.

findings.highlight: served to increase my persuasiveness
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のこの態度に、説得力を持たせてしまっていた
findings.explanation: The obvious wrong Haruki did Setsuna makes his excessive apologetic behavior look convincingly explained, thereby camouflaging the deeper betrayal. He is not becoming more persuasive in an argument.
findings.japanese:
雪菜にそんなに酷いことをしてしまった事実が、
俺のこの態度に、説得力を持たせてしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: The fact that I've done something so horrible to Setsuna only served to increase my persuasiveness.

findings.highlight: I'd consider her declaration a bit selfish
findings.evidenceJa: いつもなら、もう少しワガママを言ったかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki observes that under ordinary circumstances Setsuna herself might have made a slightly more selfish demand. The translation instead has Haruki judge her present, conspicuously considerate words as selfish.
findings.japanese: いつもなら、もう少しワガママを言ったかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: Normally, I'd consider her declaration a bit selfish.

findings.highlight: a parent who can cheer you up just by being around you
findings.evidenceJa: 一緒にいてもいいって気にさせてくれる親なんだぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki says Youko is a parent who makes Kazusa feel that it is all right for them to be together. 'Cheer you up just by being around' replaces the hard-won permission for continued family intimacy with a generic mood benefit.
findings.japanese:
「それでも一緒にいること、お前全然嫌がってないだろ。
一緒にいてもいいって気にさせてくれる親なんだぞ？
お前、その価値全然認めないつもりか？」
findings.todokanai: "Yet you don't mind being with her at all, do you? She's a parent who can cheer you up just by being around you. You don't plan on recognizing the value in that?"

findings.highlight: as if attempting to persuade her
findings.evidenceJa: まるで口説いているかのようにかずさをカメラのレンズ越しに視姦してる
findings.explanation: The photographer is talking as though trying to seduce Kazusa while visually undressing or violating her through the lens. 'Persuade' strips the explicitly sexual register from both 口説く and 視姦.
findings.japanese:
そして今は、こちらも３０分遅れて到着した
現地のカメラマンが、まるで口説いているかのように
かずさをカメラのレンズ越しに視姦してる。
findings.todokanai: And now the cameraman, who himself arrived 30 minutes late, is ogling at Kazusa through the camera lens, as if attempting to persuade her.

findings.highlight: it seems you rejected her
findings.evidenceJa: わたしのコンサートチケット送ったのに、結局、ふられちゃったわね
findings.explanation: Youko says that although she sent Haruki a ticket to her concert, he ultimately stood her up; his was the sole empty front-row seat. 'Rejected her' falsely points the action toward Kazusa and obscures Youko's own invitation.
findings.japanese:
「だからわたしのコンサートチケット送ったのに、
結局、ふられちゃったわね。
…最前列で空いてたのはあなたの席だけだったわよ」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I sent you a concert ticket, but in the end, it seems you rejected her… After all, your seat was the only one that was empty in the front row."

findings.highlight: win time after time in famous competitions
findings.evidenceJa: 世界中の権威あるコンクールを勝ち抜く腕
findings.explanation: Kazusa has acquired the skill to fight her way through prestigious competitions worldwide, not a record of repeatedly winning them. The overstatement conflicts with her much-discussed fourth-place finish.
findings.japanese:
だから、五年間頑張ってきたかずさは、
世界中の権威あるコンクールを勝ち抜く腕と、
強い意志を手に入れた。
findings.todokanai: That's why Kazusa's been able to win time after time in famous competitions after working so hard for five years. She's gained a strong will.

findings.highlight: She had the talent from the start.
findings.evidenceJa: 富は、もともとあった
findings.explanation: Kazusa originally had wealth; she later acquired fame herself. Translating 富 as talent erases the wealth/fame pair and repeats an artistic endowment already established elsewhere.
findings.japanese:
富は、もともとあった。
名声は、自分で手に入れた。
findings.todokanai: She had the talent from the start. She gained renown with her own hands.

findings.highlight: No matter what happens… and no matter what the reason…
findings.evidenceJa: だからどうだって訳でも…どうしようって訳でも、ないんだけど
findings.explanation: Haruki tells himself that their final separation does not mean anything in particular and that he does not intend to do anything about it. The English does not express either proposition and is incoherent with the sentence fragment that follows.
findings.japanese:
だからどうだって訳でも…
どうしようって訳でも、ないんだけど…
findings.todokanai: No matter what happens… and no matter what the reason…

findings.highlight: Kazusa's outstretched right foot
findings.evidenceJa: かずさが軽く右足を引きずってみせた
findings.explanation: Kazusa demonstrates by lightly dragging or limping on her injured right foot. She does not merely stretch it out; the visible limp is what reminds Haruki why she cannot use the piano pedal.
findings.japanese:
かずさが軽く右足を引きずってみせたのと同時に、
何もかも吹っ飛んでた記憶が一気に蘇る。
findings.todokanai: At the sight of Kazusa's outstretched right foot, all the memories that had left me return in an instant.

findings.highlight: who couldn't even choose her in the end
findings.evidenceJa: 結果としてしか雪菜を選べなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki condemns himself because he could choose Setsuna only as the eventual result—after remaining with Kazusa until time forced his return. The English says he did not choose Setsuna even in the end, reversing the tortured distinction on which his self-indictment rests.
findings.japanese:
結果としてしか雪菜を選べなかった、
こんな、最低な…
findings.todokanai: This horrible person, who couldn't even choose her in the end…
